title: Parity lies in log-depth circuit complexity
statement: The language of Boolean lists containing an odd number of true entries is recognized by a family of acyclic Boolean circuits with fan-in at most two, size bounded by a polynomial in the input length, and depth bounded by a constant multiple of $\log_2 n+1$. In other words, parity belongs to the class defined by these conditions with depth exponent $1$.
